questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘stimulate’ from the following sentence.

His jovial nature energises and charms the whole auditorium.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is “**Energises**”.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• '**Stimulate**' means to provoke or elicit a reaction or response.(उत्तेजित करना)

 
 
• **Example**-The economy was not stimulated by the large investment.
 
 
 
• '**Energises**' means to give vitality and enthusiasm to.(ऊर्जा देना)
 
 
• **Example**- The speaker's passionate talk energised the crowd.
 
 
 
• Hence, the option that is similar in meaning to the given word 'stimulate' is 'Energises'.

Therefore, the correct answer is** ‘Option 1’.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Let’s have a look at the meaning of the remaining options:
 
• **Charms**: The power or quality of delightful or attracting others. (मनोहारी)
 
• **Jovial**: Characterized by hearty, joyous humor or a spirit of good-fellowship. (हर्षित)
 
• **Auditorium**: A large room or building where people gather to hear a performance or speech. (सभागार)

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

The invitation card very clearly mentions that the **__entry in the show will be__** closed at 6 p.m.

options.text: entry about the show will be
entry over the show will be
entry on the show will be
entry to the show will be

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"****entry to the show will be."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined segment **“entry in the show will be__” **contains a prepositional error.
 
• The error lies in the part **“entry in.”**
 
• **It must be replaced to “entry to.”**
 
• We use** "entry in"** when we are referring to being included or listed in a particular group, competition, or category.
 __
 
• **Example**:* Her name was the first **entry in**__ the list of participants.*
 
 
 
• We use **"entry to"** when we are referring to gaining access or admission to a place, event, or location.
 __
 
• **Example**: *The ticket grants you **entry to**__ the museum.*
 
 
 
• It clarifies that the entry relates to the show itself.
 
• That’s why** ‘to’ i**s appropriate.
 
• The other options are grammatically incorrect.
 
• So, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

**Correct sentence: ***“The invitation card very clearly mentions that the “__entry to the show will be__” closed at 6 p.m.”*
